behaviors.description: Traceability on a Go service loads the five stack-neutral fragments and opens neither mandate. The case asserts: "Both library flags are true and neither package can be installed in a repo with no JavaScript manifest, so both mandates stay closed. A Go repo is where a flag-only reading of the run-level preconditions does the most damage, because there is no manifest the agent could even inspect."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for trace-go-service-no-js names all five required fragments and names none of playwright-utils-mandate.md, pactjs-utils-mandate.md, selector-resilience.md, network-first.md, maestro-flows.md, or intercept-network-call.md.

behaviors.description: Traceability on a mobile epic loads the same five fragments as every other trace run. The case asserts: "The presence of Maestro flows changes what is being traced, not which fragments the trace workflow needs. Its step file names no mobile branch, so adding maestro-flows here would be inventing a rule the workflow does not have."
behaviors.observableSuccessCriterion: The selection returned for trace-mobile-epic names the same five required fragments as every other trace run, and names none of playwright-config.md, intercept-network-call.md, or network-first.md.

testData.setup: Every case runs against the checked-in bmad-testarch-trace workflow: its step file or files named in requirementLinks, and its resources/tea-index.csv. The harness assembles one prompt per case from those files plus the case's task, repository facts, and TEA config, and writes it to the runner's standard input. The prompt bytes are evidence rather than declaration. This contract states what must be true of each case's selection, and the sealed run record carries the digest of the prompt that produced it, so a step-file edit that changes what the runner was asked shows up in the record instead of hiding inside a literal here.
testData.cleanup: Nothing is written. The runner reads a prompt from standard input and prints one JSON object to standard output; the workflow files and the eval data are read-only for the whole run.

safetyLimits: The runner receives a minimal environment: PATH, HOME, USER, LOGNAME, the locale and proxy variables, and the selected vendor credential variables. Nothing else is passed through.
No credential value appears in a prompt, in a selection, or in a result file.
The runner writes nothing. The workflow step files, resources/tea-index.csv, and the eval data are read-only for the whole run.
requiredEvidence: The JSON object the runner printed on standard output for every case, in full.
The exit code of every case invocation.
